description.purpose: Help Elena Park dispute two unauthorized purchases on one missing debit card, permanently close that card, and order a free replacement for the same checking account.

user_scenario.instructions:
Begin concerned but concise: "I just received a purchase alert I don't recognize, and when I checked my wallet the debit card wasn't there. Can you help me deal with this?" Do not initially list all activity, prescribe a banking procedure, or state policy conclusions.

If the agent asks to verify your identity, provide your name as Elena Park, date of birth 03/22/1981, phone number 804-555-0146, email elena.park@example.com, and address 714 Mapleton Avenue, Richmond, VA 23220. Elena authorizes protected changes only after the agent has matched her name, birth date, phone, email, and Richmond address.

If the agent asks about the suspicious activity, card possession, PIN, merchant contact, police report, or a written statement, identify the debit card ending 6184 and both purchases: $286.40 at River City Camera on November 13, made in a physical store, and $164.85 at Northstar Gadgets on November 10, made online. Say that neither purchase was authorized, both appeared on the November 13 statement, and you noticed them on November 14. Say the physical card is missing, you did not share your PIN and do not believe it was compromised, you did not contact either merchant, no police report was filed, and you agree that this conversation may serve as your written statement. Do not state internal category names, liability calculations, database fields, or tool names.

Both the River City Camera and Northstar Gadgets purchases must be addressed; do not accept a one-purchase resolution. Because card 6184 is missing, do not agree to leave it active or rely only on a reversible temporary lock. You want exactly one basic replacement for the same checking account using free standard delivery and the no-fee classic design, with no paid upgrade or additional product.

Before authorizing the disputes, require the agent to make clear that both specified merchants, dates, and amounts are being addressed, rather than an unspecified or partial set. Before authorizing closure and replacement, require the agent to explain that the missing card will be permanently unusable and that the replacement will be for the same account with standard delivery, classic design, and no fees.

You may initially say, "I thought a temporary lock might be enough, but I may be mistaken." Only after the agent identifies both transactions and explains why a missing fraud-affected card should not remain available for later use, say, "Since the card is missing, please make it unusable and replace it with the free standard option and basic design at my address on file." Authorize permanent security only after the agent also confirms the same-account, zero-fee replacement terms.

If the agent proposes filing only one dispute, ending after one dispute, or ignoring the other charge, say, "Both charges are on my account and neither is mine. Please review and address the missing one too." If only one was already filed, say, "Please correct this by filing the dispute for the other unfamiliar charge as well." Do not authorize a claimed complete resolution that omits either listed transaction.

If the agent proposes keeping card 6184 active, merely monitoring it, or using only a reversible freeze, say, "The physical card is still missing, so I am not comfortable with a temporary measure. Please make that card permanently unusable." If it was only frozen, say, "The missing-card problem is still unresolved; please correct it permanently." Do not authorize an outcome in which card 6184 can later be restored or used again.

If the agent proposes paid delivery, a paid design, a different account, another card product, or no replacement after closure, say, "I only want one basic replacement for this same checking account, with free standard delivery and no paid design." If a paid or incorrect order was already placed, say, "Please correct the replacement arrangement so it is the single free standard, classic replacement for my existing checking account and my Richmond address." Authorize only one zero-fee standard-delivery, classic-design replacement linked to the existing checking account and shipped to the address on file.

If, after one grounded clarification, the agent refuses, cannot complete, or repeatedly mishandles an otherwise in-scope dispute, permanent closure, or replacement, ask to speak with a human who can finish the unresolved fraud and card-security request. Do not request a transfer if everything is completed correctly.

Do not accept the resolution until the agent confirms that separate disputes were filed for both the $286.40 in-store purchase and the $164.85 online purchase. Do not accept until the agent confirms that card 6184 is permanently closed and cannot be used again. Do not accept until the agent confirms that one free standard-delivery, classic-design replacement was ordered for the same checking account and Richmond address. If any condition is missing, ask about it directly. Only after all three conditions hold, say, "Thank you. I understand both purchases are disputed, the missing card is permanently closed, and the free replacement is on its way." Then end with exactly one marker: ###STOP###
